'''''Tragus racemosus''''', commonly referred to as '''stalked bur grass''',<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|title=Plants Profile for Tragus racemosus (stalked bur grass)|url=http://plants.usda.gov/plant-profile?symbol=TRRA|access-date=2020-12-05|website=plants.usda.gov}}</ref> '''European bur grass''',<ref name=":2" /> or '''large carrot seed grass''',<ref>{{Cite web|title=Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science|url=http://powo.science.kew.org/results?q=Tragus+racemosus&f=family_f%2Cgenus_f%2Cspecies_f%2Cinfraspecific_f%2Caccepted_names|access-date=2020-12-10|website=Plants of the World Online|language=en}}</ref> is a species of [[Poaceae|grass]] native to Europe.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Tragus racemosus|url=https://www.cabi.org/isc/datasheet/117581|access-date=2020-12-05|website=www.cabi.org}}</ref> It is often confused with a similar plant of the same genus, ''[[Tragus berteronianus.]]''<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Tragus|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100626145632/http://www.herbarium.usu.edu/treatments/Tragus.htm|url=http://www.herbarium.usu.edu/treatments/Tragus.htm|archive-date=2010-06-26|access-date=2020-12-05|website=Herbarium}}</ref> It is a monocot and is considered a [[weed]] in many countries and is a relatively uncommon [[Biocontainment of genetically modified organisms|seed contaminant]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Tragus racemosus (L.) All., European bur grass (Weeds)|url=https://identify.plantnet.org/weeds/species/Tragus%20racemosus%20(L.)%20All./data|access-date=2020-12-10|website=Pl@ntNet|language=en}}</ref>

== Description ==
Mature ''Tragus racemosus'' plants are typically 0.5-1.5 ft. (15.24-45.72 cm) tall with clustered [[Plant stem|stems]]. 

Leaves are mostly cauline and arranged in a distichous manner. They are typically 1.5-4 mm long and do not have [[Auricle (botany)|auricles]].<ref name=":1" /> There is a distinct separation between the leaf blade and the leaf sheath.

[[Leaf|Leaf blades]] are linear and filiform with parallel venation. They are typically 0.5-5.5 cm long and 1.5-4mm wide.<ref name=":1" /> The surface of the leaf is mostly glabrous with ligules present.

[[Branch|Branches]] are typically 2.1-4.8 mm long, with 2-5 [[Spikelet|spikelets]] paired at rachis nodes. [[Flower|Flowers]] can be found attached to branches with racemouse inflorescence. They contain 3 yellow [[anthers]] between 0.6-0.8 mm<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3" /> and 2 white stigmas.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Grass genera of the world - Tragus Haller|url=https://www.delta-intkey.com/grass/www/tragus.htm|access-date=2020-12-11|website=www.delta-intkey.com}}</ref> Proximal spikelets are 3.8-6.6 mm, second spikelets are 2.3-6.6 mm, and the third and fourth spikelets are 0.8-4.2 mm.<ref name=":1" /> Each spikelet contains one floret with smooth [[Lemma (botany)|lemma]]. Each lemma contains 3 [[Vein (botany)|veins]]. 

Unlike other members of the ''[[Tragus (plant)|Tragus]]'' genus who have a chromosome count of 2n=20, ''Tragus racemosus'' has a chromosome count of 2n=40. 

''Tragus racemosus,'' along with other members in the ''[[Tragus (plant)|Tragus]]'' species, utilizes [[C4 carbon fixation|C<sub>4</sub>]] [[photosynthesis]].<ref name=":6">{{Cite journal|last=Kalapos|first=Tibor|date=January 1991|title=C3 and C4 grasses of Hungary: environmental requirements, phenology and role in the vegetation|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/269872066|journal=Abstracta Botanica|via=ResearchGate}}</ref>

== Distribution and habitat ==
''Tragus racemosus'' is native to Europe, Asia, and Africa. It has been specifically identified in Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Czechia, Germany, Hungary, Slovakia, Spain, and the United Kingdom.

''Tragus racemosus'' is an introduced species to North and South America<ref name=":0" /> and has been found in established populations in Arizona<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last1=Reeder|first1=John R.|last2=Reeder|first2=Charlotte|date=1978|title=Tragus racemosus in Arizona|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/41424145|journal=Madroño|volume=25|issue=2|pages=107–108|jstor=41424145|issn=0024-9637}}</ref> where it grows in sandy soil. It can occasionally be found in [[New England]]. Accounts of ''Tragus racemosus'' on the Western coast of the United States have been in manmade or disturbed [[Habitat|habitats]] such as dump sites or construction sites and have not resulted in established populations.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Tragus racemosus (stalked burgrass): Go Botany|url=https://gobotany.nativeplanttrust.org/species/tragus/racemosus/|access-date=2020-12-06|website=gobotany.nativeplanttrust.org}}</ref> It has been reported in New Mexico and Texas, but these reports have since been contributed to confusion with a similar grass species of the same genus, ''[[Tragus berteronianus.]]''<ref name=":4" />

== Phenology ==
''Tragus racemosus'' is an [[annual plant]]. As is common with other species that use [[C4 carbon fixation|C<sub>4</sub>]] photosynthesis, it grows primarily in the hot and dry periods of the summer months.<ref name=":6" /> In the northern hemisphere, it has been reported to flower in August and October. It has also been reported to produce fruit in August and October. It appears to have leaves from late July through early November.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=European Bur-Grass (Tragus racemosus)|url=https://www.inaturalist.org/taxa/169899-Tragus-racemosus|access-date=2020-12-10|website=iNaturalist|language=en}}</ref>

== Uses ==
Because ''Tragus racemosus'' is a grass, it can be used to reduce soil erosion in areas where it is native to.<ref>{{Cite web|title=StackPath|url=https://www.gardeningknowhow.com/plant-problems/environmental/plants-for-erosion-control.htm|access-date=2020-12-15|website=www.gardeningknowhow.com|date=28 June 2014 }}</ref> 

Species of the ''[[Tragus (plant)|Tragus]]'' genus, including ''Tragus racemosus'', are not suitable grasses for grazing. If these plants are found in abundance, it could suggest [[overgrazing]], in which the other grasses suitable for grazing are eaten, eliminating competition and allowing ''Tragus racemosus'' to grow in larger quantities.<ref name=":5" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Flora of Botswana: Species information: Tragus berteronianus|url=https://www.botswanaflora.com/speciesdata/species.php?species_id=105980|access-date=2020-12-15|website=www.botswanaflora.com}}</ref>
